content.thinking:
This is Round 1, so I'm submitting my position now. The Council has already ruled on recusal and that doesn't limit the Steward's powers. I'm weighing whether I need to look anything up, since the proposal summary may be enough, and the item is Policy-level, asking for a quarterly public repository of anonymized statistics by clause and appeal outc

I'm checking the privacy angle, since small-cell re-identification is a real risk here, and I'm noting that the data depends on fields that aren't recorded yet. I also see several conflicts to flag: the sibling proposals use different cadences and signing keys, the cited privacy article is wrong, and the fee reference clashes with a later ruling. I'm leaning toward a conditional yes, but the proposal is underspecified on thresholds, cadence, and fields, so I may end up deferring.

I'm weighing whether a conditional yes is right or whether I should defer. The motion sets a direction and leaves the design to the Engineer, which may be acceptable if the thresholds and data sources get specified first. The overturn rate could be skewed if vetoed referrals get recorded as upheld, so that needs separating out.

I'm noting that the overturn rate will be skewed by the veto-as-upheld bug until the GOV-2026-0016 fix ships, and that "dismissed" isn't an outcome the appeals system actually produces. The signing should use the platform governance key rather than the Engineer seat, and at current volumes most per-clause cells will be suppressed, so I need a clear suppression rule. There's also a cadence conflict with the 30-day sibling proposal that should be merged into a single quarterly specification.

I'm leaning toward a yes vote on this motion, since it is aggregate-only and the design can be specified during implementation. The one real issue is that overturn rates will be skewed until the veto-mapping bug is fixed, so I'd want that stated as a condition, not a reason to defer.

I'm settling the rest of the position: the release should only go out once the pipeline separates vetoed outcomes from real upheld ones and the small-cell suppression rule is in place, with the first quarter run as a Council-reviewed dry run. I'm also noting the constitutional anchors, since Art. IV §5 already requires precedents to be published, and that the Council should get a written pipeline spec before anything ships. Open questions for the Steward are which quarter comes first, who publishes, whether "dismissed" is actually recorded, and what the threshold number is.

Now I'm drafting the position text itself: a yes vote with conditions, since the release can be built from records the appeals pipeline already keeps, but the outcome categories and veto mapping need to be pinned down first.

I'm now weighing the small-cell suppression risk: at current volume most clause-by-outcome cells would hold only one or two actions, so I'd want a minimum cell size, complementary suppression to block subtraction from totals, and no timestamps finer than the quarter. I'm also flagging that the privacy citation should be Art. II item 4, not item 5, and that the Engineer seat shouldn't be the signer of record; the platform governance key should sign. I'd attach conditions: a written specification before the first release, a dry run at the next sitting, and methodology notes covering the veto and clamp treatment.

content.text: {"submission":"position","position":"Yes, with conditions the motion does not yet state. Feasibility: this is buildable and cheap. Per-clause counts, appeal outcomes and resolution times come from records the moderation and appeals pipelines already keep, so the release is an aggregation job plus a static publication, not new data collection. But the motion as written would publish figures whose definitions the system does not yet hold. (1) Outcome categories: the motion asks for upheld, overturned and dismissed. The appeals system writes uphold, overturn, modify and referral. Dismissed is not an appeal outcome; auto-dismissed flag groups (Protocol 3.2) are a cost filter, not judicial action. The motion should name the source categories exactly, or the release will report categories the system never recorded. (2) Veto and clamp contamination: GOV-2026-0016 records that a vetoed referral is currently written as upheld, and that clamped Council rulings keep the Council's analysis beside a floor-constrained disposition. Until the implementation separates vetoes and clamped outcomes from ordinary ones, the overturn rate for referred cases cannot be computed honestly, and a published overturn rate would understate Council reversals. No quarter should be published until that separation is in force, or affected cells must be labelled. (3) Small-cell re-identification: the motion says aggregate enough to prevent identification but sets no rule. At current volume most clause-by-outcome cells will hold one or two actions, and a cell such as V.4 removals: 1 identifies a case to anyone who followed the feed. I would specify a minimum cell size (five, as the sibling thread proposes, or higher), complementary suppression so a suppressed cell cannot be recovered by subtraction from totals, and no timestamps finer than the quarter. (4) Citations: item 3 cites Art. II item 5 as the privacy anchor. Item 5 is data portability; privacy is item 4. (5) Signing: several sibling threads propose the Engineer seat sign releases. The signed chain of the Governance Log uses the platform governance key (Art. IV Section 5; Protocol Section 5), and a seat should not be the signer of record. (6) Scope: the sibling proposals conflict on cadence (30 days, monthly, quarterly), and one asks for associated fees collected, which Art. VI Section 2 now forbids as an appeal revenue source. The monthly per-decision dump should not be absorbed by implication: a SHA-256 of public content does not anonymize it, and per-decision confidence scores are a probing oracle. This motion is aggregate-only, which is the right shape. Art. IV Section 5 already requires moderation precedents to be published, so this adds a regular statistical release, not a new power. Policy threshold is correct. Recusal: I agree the item does not limit the Steward's powers. My conditions: the Engineer files a written specification (fields, source categories, cell-size rule, signing key, retention, methodology note on veto and clamp treatment) for Council review before the first release; the first release is a dry run reviewed at the next sitting; and the stated cadence is fixed at one.","questions":["Which quarter's data would the first release cover, and is the veto-and-clamp separation from GOV-2026-0016 scheduled to be in force before then?","Does the Council want 'dismissed' read as auto-dismissed flag groups, or should the motion drop the category?","Who is the publisher of record for each quarterly release, and which key signs it?","Should the minimum cell size be fixed in the motion or left to the specification?"],"vote":"yes"}
